summary: A switch for an on/off setting, with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the switch and its accessible name. Required: an external <label for> cannot name the inner control.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when the row has other visible text naming the switch.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid and blocks form submission.

value.note: Submitted with the form while on.

checked.note: Current state (on). Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Native required: must be on to be valid. Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Native disabled; dimmed; not submitted. Also applied by a disabled fieldset ancestor without changing this attribute.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: switch in the first column, label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Track wrapper; positions the thumb over the native input.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">; receives focus, Space and validation. Painted as the track.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: The knob; slides to the end side when on and follows the writing direction.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring and border in ring color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track takes the primary fill and the thumb moves to the end.

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute or disabled fieldset ancestor

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: FormAssociated mixin with NativeControl. formValue(): value only while checked, else null. formReset(): restores the checked attribute default. formStateRestore(): restores checked. validationAnchor(): the inner input, whose required gives valueMissing. disabled (own or fieldset) is not submitted. Error sets a customError validity (SB-0009).

accessibility.targetSize: Track is 32x20 (default) or 24x16 (sm); the label next to it is part of the clickable row and the 12px gap relies on the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception. A hidden label leaves only the track as target, so hide-label is limited to rows with other clickable text.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px ring in switch.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: move focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009). Does not toggle.

aria: role="switch" on the native checkbox exposes aria-checked from its checked state
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
on/off is not conveyed by color or thumb position alone: the state is in the accessibility tree and the on track also differs in luminance from the off track
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: An on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it is flipped
The setting is submitted with a form
The consequence of turning it on needs explaining

antiPatterns.pattern: A yes/no choice that is only recorded when the form is submitted, or choosing several from a list
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as an immediate setting; a recorded choice reads as a checkbox

antiPatterns.pattern: A button that stays pressed to show a mode or format
antiPatterns.why: A switch is a form control with a value; a pressed button is an action with a state

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing exactly one option from several
antiPatterns.why: A switch has two states for one setting

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern)?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes: APG switch pattern on a native checkbox with role=switch; layout as Checkbox.
openQuestions.answer: Yes. Taken with the recommendation; no approver available in this session (SB-0011).

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.recommendation: No, as in Checkbox: the attribute is the default that form reset restores.
openQuestions.answer: No. checked is a property; the attribute is the reset default and is read at start.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes, like Checkbox and Input. hide-label keeps it as the accessible name.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes, and how are they named?
openQuestions.recommendation: default and sm, as in shadcn/ui Switch; the registered size aliases map them to medium and small.
openQuestions.answer: default (32x20 track, 16px thumb) and sm (24x16 track, 12px thumb), from the existing size.switch.* tokens.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch?
openQuestions.recommendation: No. The APG makes Enter optional; the native checkbox ignores it, and form controls submit on Enter (SB-0009). Space toggles.
openQuestions.answer: No. Enter submits the form, as Checkbox does.

openQuestions.question: Is there an indeterminate state?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: a switch is binary (APG switch has only on and off).

openQuestions.question: How does the error message relate to validity?
openQuestions.recommendation: As in Checkbox: setting error marks the field invalid, sets a customError validity and shows the message in a polite live region (SB-0009).

openQuestions.question: Is a native checkbox with role=switch acceptable for the inner control?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes: native semantics first (SB-0007); role=switch exposes on/off and the native control keeps Space, focus, required and validity.
openQuestions.answer: Yes. Browser support for the switch role on checkboxes is the baseline of the supported browsers.
